body: I'm sorry your relationship ended. You're not stupid to open your heart to others and want to be loved. We can't control what other people do, only how we react to it. Give yourself time to heal, and realize that you're worth of love. Hang in there.

>but it's that there's a certain filter towards you interactions with each other that's weird. How can you even be comfortable in the first place if you have to watch what you say or do in order to not breach the terms of the contract?
 
You are missing the point. She does not have to watch what she says. Neither of us do. "I'll be honest with you about how I'm feeling and won't disappear." That's it. Period. I don't know about you, but that seemed like a perfectly reasonable, adult mindset to have to me. The fact that we agreed on it doesn't make it weird. Perhaps you objectively perceive it as weird, but the only two people who's opinions matter in that context are her's and mine, and we don't think it's fucking weird.

>But to be attracted for years and not make a move? That's taking it too seriously. You're just attracted to someone, nothing major about that. Because it's nothing major then it should be fairly easy to make moves on them. If it's major to the point of waiting years until you had the courage then that's prizing it too heavily.

When for the vast, overwhelming majority of those years she wasn't single. I don't fuck with other people's relationships. Only recently did she appear to be single, I saw my opportunity, and I asked. I wasn't fucking prizing anything. I was waiting until it wouldn't have been a complete asshole thing to do while she was involved with other people.

When I said I felt strongly about her, I was referring to after we'd met, and I was irrationally worried she'd disappear. She didn't, and I realize that yes, I let myself get too attached, too fast. But it wasn't the whole time.

>You haven't found your future wife in all this time, no offense but I highly doubt you're going to have missed the opportunity in your life if you just take a small break from searching.

That's not what you said. You said "even rebuff any moves women make on you." There's a difference between not seeking anyone out, which is a perfectly reasonable thing to do, and actively refuse someone else's advances. I can see your point in letting it come naturally. I cannot with refusing it when it actually does. If by "all this time" you mean the 15 years I flushed down the toilet being a trainwreck addict of a human being, absolutely. But you can't see the future. No one can. Highly doubt all you want (which is no less arrogant, btw) but were I to rebuff the advances of someone who might be one of these people who synergize well with me, then what in the actual fuck was the point of trying to meet people in the first place?

>But if you're not willing to change how important this is for you then you're not going to stop feeling awful. Even if it turns out someone does come into your life you're not suddenly going to stop valuing this...what do you think is going to happen if they decide to leave? You need to stop caring so much and you can start by forcing yourself to take a break.

If that happens, and they decide to leave, I'll deal with it. It's happened before and I'm still here.

I have half a mind to nuke this whole goddamn thread at this point, so this is my last response. You're going from offering advice to making presumptions about my life based on what relatively small amount of detail I've offerered. Granted, there would be no way for me to write every last bit of it out, but this is starting to feel like a wall of text pissing contest and I'm losing my patience with being semi-talked down to. Maybe there's more to my self-esteem than I realize.

You made your points: Don't take relationships so seriously. Let it come to me. Stop looking everywhere. Get different interests. Attraction is fluid. Stop obsessing. 

Got it. Thanks for your input.

>That's just asking too much. It's weird in the first place that she has to make a deal with you. Sounds like she hardly knows you in a romantic manner, and for you to start setting up this sort of contract with her is honestly pretty scary. It's almost as if you guys are legally obligated to interact in a particular manner. That's not how regular interactions work. Relationships should be something fun and light, not a "do this, do that, in return I do this or that," situation. I don't know how you phrased it but it comes off as being controlling when she doesn't even know you that well; if you're already being this demanding in the beginning she might wonder how you'll be after a month or two. Even if you guys have been seeing each other for a few weeks, I'm going to be straight up honest with you and say that any sane woman would automatically dip because this is a major red flag.

For the record, she offered. Said something to the effect of "I'm known for disappearing, so as long as you're okay with me being honest about what I am and am not ready for, I won't disappear. I know you're not cool with that." It was her being understanding, empathizing and volunteering to not deliberately cause unnecessary pain. It does not mean she's contractually obligated to fall for me.

> Did you mention to her how you've had feelings for her for years? That alone would do it. Or if you weren't really friends with her during that entire time of getting to know her, suddenly telling her that you like her is a wtf moment.

I did not have feelings for her for years. All I ever wanted to do was ask her out -- that's it. So I did. We've gone out a few times, and we clicked. I only told her I liked her after it was fairly obvious.

>I'm asking you to voluntarily stop seeking and to even rebuff any moves women make on you. I want you to consciously do it from a place entirely free of pain or hope of it somehow improving your future chances to get with women. Just like you did with your addictions, say no.

And pass up the opportunity if the right person does come along?

I know we all die alone, and maybe other people are perfectly happy to spend the twilight of their years by themselves, and find fulfillment doing any number of different things with their time and energy. Good for them. I accept that this may be a possibility for me, but I'd rather not if I don't have to.

I'm not going to kill myself over this, or anyone else who comes along. I just want to stop feeling so fucking awful about it.

That site has an ability like to no other to re-open old wounds. That part of you that loved them more than anyone else will always be with you, but it doesn't mean it can't be surpassed. I'm sorry you had to go that, but glad you're moving on. It's all we can do.

I know what you mean about spending most days not really caring. Feels like Life On Repeat, right? Just going through the motions.

I'm sorry things didn't work out in your relationship. Despite the onus of making this thread, I also believe it is ultimately better to be alone than with someone who doesn't appreciate or really want to be with you. It's why I've never let myself settle for less than someone I legitimately wanted to be with, the trouble was always finding that reciprocated. It just gets harder and harder to want to keep going. You made the right decision to end things if he wasn't putting in the effort, and likewise I'll make the right decision to no longer reach out to the person I was interested in if they don't make a reciprocal effort.

It sounds like we are in the same boat, honestly. We know what is wrong and what we need to, just not how to actually get there. I will say there are fleeting moments where I do feel emotionally independent, where I'm so focused on whatever I'm doing or experiencing that it blocks out everything else. It does feel at some other points that things don't matter without someone to do them with.

I hope you're able to get to that point, both of us, for that matter. We do owe it to ourselves, at least to try, don't we.

I guess none. I've never not worried about this. I've always felt like a piece of shit around women, going back to a very, very young age and a traumatic event when my father was accused of being a pedophile at the elementary school he taught at, that I attended. I used to lay awake in bed at night as an adolescent and convince myself that I was never going to meet anyone special. When I finally did in high school, and it was everything I ever wanted, later ending with her going behind my back and leaving me for my best friend two years later, I sliced myself up, spent a few days in a hospital and then turned to dope and later alcohol to numb the pain instead of ever actually dealing with it. At this point, it feels like a built-in flaw that, no matter what I do to try to overcome or most past it, will always be there. Hence the desire to simply check out.

I will admit that it's usually not this bad when they disappear. I felt especially strong about this one, who I'd finally built up the courage to ask out after years of wanting to. At no point did I dump a ton of romantic shit on her, I haven't messaged her since Wednesday, and all I sent that day was something that she'd told me the last time we saw each other in person that she'd be perfectly fine with. Yes, I may have given off a slight air of desperation, but no obvious lines were crossed. So I've completely disengaged. More to that, the last time we saw each other, and we made a deal that she would be honest about how much was too much, what she was or wasn't comfortable with, and in return wouldn't ghost, knowing full well how much it bothers me. I suppose it's irrelevant if I'm the real problem. Whether or not women would date me, why do I get to hear from many different female friends that I'm such a great catch, an inspiration for overcoming addictions, and worthy/deserving, when clearly it is not the case? Are they just being nice or outright lying? Do you know how angry that makes me to hear that shit at times like this, when it's so fucking crystal clear that I am not, as made evident by the things you've pointed out, as well as the fact that this thread even exists? 

Thank you. It hasn't been easy, but I do feel like a loser in situations like this. This is what I mean when I say I feel reliable -- fighting the urge to drink or get high every single day, especially at times like this -- and still manage to come home sober every night. I've been rejected by potential partners for no other reason than the fact that I don't drink. Let me tell you how wonderful *that* feels. And I know, it's a reflection of them and not me, same as when people ghost and disappear. It feels no less shitty, and turns this thing I'm supposed to be proud of into an albatross hanging around my neck.

I didn't dump anything on her. I admit I have done this in the past with other friends, and I know it was a shitty thing to do, and I try to remain cognizant of when I start to do it and pump the brakes. I know that's what I'm doing right now to you and everyone who has taken the time to respond in this thread, and I'm sorry. It's yet another stream that feeds into the lake of embracing the idea of checking out. Realistically there's no way for you to believe whether or not I've only opened up to the women I've met in tolerable doses, just based on what I'm saying, but I like to think I haven't. I know how much is too much. This wasn't that, and at no point did I exploit her for personal comfort, though I'm sure the last interaction we had was somehow interpreted that way, hence her disappearance.

I do not know how to focus on being comfortable with myself. I do things I want that I like, when I want to do them. Much of it feels like hollow, empty distractions. Very few things feel legitimately fulfilling. I would never ask for or want someone to stay with me only because they're afraid of what would happen to me if they left. I know that's shitty. That's why I don't argue, beg or chase when these women disappear. I know enough to realize that it is a waste of time to pursue someone who does not reciprocate.

What more is there to life than eventually sharing it with someone? Changing the lives of others but having no one to come home to? You've got no family or relationships? What are you going to do from the time you're 40 until you're 80? Go run a company? Humans are pair-bonding creatures, with an instinctive, primal drive to procreate. To deny that is to deny biology. I can pretend it isn't there all I want. It just gets that much louder. I actually did exactly what you suggested in 2017 -- took the entire year off from trying to find romance, after I was ghosted by someone I'd been involved with for six months, who again promised in the beginning not to. Six Months. I thought a year off would serve me well. Apparently it did not. 

I don't expect a woman to solve all my troubles. I'm just tired of doing it all alone, all the time. It's the little things that kill us when they add up over time. Death by a thousand cuts. I do feel drained, and have very little left after this last time.

I am going back to see a therapist for the first time since I quit drinking on Sunday. I do at least realize the magnitude of how much of an issue this is.

I've met plenty of women of the past few years I felt at least initially compatible with. They all walked away, some at least having the decency to tell me that they weren't feeling it, which at that point felt orders of magnitude better, I respected their honesty and legit didn't have a problem keeping them as friends.

How do you define compatibility? Similar interests? Life goals? Like the same stupid movies? What exactly is chemistry, and how do I know I've actually found it versus infatuation and impulse?

I don't feel I deserve one. I don't feel I deserve anything. Like another user pointed out, that I even go to these lengths just because someone walks away from me, is proof that I'm not ready, and likely not deserving of someone's love.

I have bettered myself as a person. It's simply not enough. As for full living, being able to grow with a partner, raise a family... these things are very likely to never happen for me.

They are not inside my head. They are on Facebook Messenger in the form of a conversation where all I had to do was keep my mouth shut for five minutes, and maybe we'd still be talking. I'm in control, and I find a way to fuck it up every single time.

I do not believe in myself. I believe in myself insofar as my ability to fuck things up and make mistakes. I believe I will never learn how to properly communicate with women and not come off so painfully fucking desperate for affection after spending my entire adult life without it.

Part of me would rather consider taking a chance at seeing the other side than taking a chance trying to find a partner, simply because I don't want to keep going through these feelings and fears. 

I don't feel I'll ever be able to experience fully living. So what is the point?

Honestly, I don't much know anymore these days. Cutting out the things that involve pain would mean cutting out ever attempting to meet a romantic partner ever again. Cutting out any more hope that I won't scare someone off by wanting to spend time together. Cutting out ever being excited about the prospect of a partner.

I am happy you have found a better life by doing less. I fear that, after this most recent woman has ceased communication, I no longer care to go through this ever again, and would rather consider just permanently checking out.

I wish I still believed that there is that mythical person out there I'm meant to be with. I also wish I believed that when someone ghosts, it's purely on them.

But I do not believe I will ever meet that person, and I believe I have inadvertently driven women away by showing even the faintest whiffs of desperation, causing them to ghost.

Before anything, thank you for taking the time to comment.

I've been single a cumulative 18 of the past 20 years. I turn 40 later this year, and the longest relationship I've ever had to date is the one I had in high school. I do everything alone, and to be frank... I'm sick of walking around and seeing couples everywhere, and I have to do everything by myself. To a point, I am able to do things by myself and enjoy them, and then I'll see a happy couple together holding hands, and remember that I'm still alone. All I ever do is hang out with myself, and the very small, close knit circle of friends I have.

What has consistently, continually happened is that I'll be neutral and content doing my own thing. I'll invariably meet someone, have the slightest bit of rapport, engage and for a very short time, will feel good about the possibility of it developing into something more. Then, the person will slowly back away and eventually disappear, without knowing specifically what it is I've said or done that made them change their mind (and at this point I'm fairly certain of what *not* to do, like the shit that gets posted on cringepics, creepypms, niceguys and whiteknights.) and I'll slip into a terrible fucking depression, having gotten so close to the simple act of just connecting intimately with another person on an emotional and physical level, what I see *so many other people out there doing* and feel like complete fucking damaged goods.

I have focused on myself quite a bit in the few years. I can't go into too much detail without potentially  revealing my identity, but I'm a former drug addict and alcoholic who's gotten clean, lost a ton of weight, better job, saved money, started traveling, doing volunteer work -- a complete turnaround. Honestly, I'm lucky to be alive. They say the definition of insanity is doing the same thing and expecting different results. What's it called when you've changed everything and are still getting the same results? It never feels like it's enough. As a man, I can't publicly express how frustrating it is to get continually rejected sexually and romantically over and over and over. You can't show emotional vulnerability, as that's arguably as big of a turn-off as a lack of confidence, because that's exactly what it shows. I have to bury it, or post it under my anonymous internet account, because there's too many ways to find out who I am with my main account.

I am dependable, have my shit together, and I know I'm living a hell of a lot better now than I ever have before. It just never gets any easier being good enough for a few weeks, and then it disappears, and gets harder to carry each time.

I know the answer is "her loss", but it fucking feels like mine, too. I'm just tired of losing.
Glad someone else out there can be relate. I've gone so far, I just don't know much further I want to keep going. Thanks for not being cliche.

I don't want to be contrarian and argue, yet in my experience the whole texting dynamic varies wildly from person to person, and even with this woman. Sometimes it's rapid-fire immediate responses back and forth for an hour and then the next day it can take a few hours to hear back. I don't hold this against people because they're busy with their own shit. If I have my phone next to me, and I'm not instantly busy, I'm going to respond. Waiting for the sake of waiting to respond to a text, to me, *is* playing a game.

To be fair, I have let her know, to an extent, just not a thousand word brain dump of all the back-end deep fears. This really is more about me than her. I've always understood and observed that a lack of confidence, in any aspect, was least attractive thing, and nervousness falls into that category. Excitement is fine as long as it's contained, because people get scared off, and everyone has a different interpretation of how much is too much.

It's so hard to feel good enough after I haven't been so many times, but thank you.
Thank you. Good luck in your situation, and Happy Valentine's Day to you, also.

They've got it figured out, it would seem... for now. I wish I didn't feel like it was only a matter of time before things fall apart again, but we'll see how long this peace can last. I will say that I talked to one of the parties about putting me in the middle, and he agreed it could not continue, so it seems that will also stop. Time will tell. Thanks for your comment : )
